title: Device
description:
The device's half: what the service writes for this device (D-038 point
2). Not part of the version.

artifacts.description:
Where published artifacts land. The single write path. On a device the
broker writes to the signed-in user's `%USERPROFILE%\Sluse Artifacts`
instead, as that user (D-031); this path is used where there is no user
token, as in LOCAL.

audit.description: Where the broker writes audit records.

boxId.description: Which box this is. Carried on every audit record.

broker.description: Where the broker listens and what certificate it presents.

endpoint.description: What the endpoint presents, and where the console listens.

environment.description:
Which environment this box runs in. Drives `not_applicable` rows in
the preflight report and is stamped on every result file, so a LOCAL
result cannot be read as saying something about identity or the guest
boundary (D-010). A fact about how the box was made, so the device's.

journalDir.description: Where the endpoint writes its per-session journal files.

maxReadBytes.description: Inline-read cap in bytes. Fixed by the product; tests lower it.

workspace.description: The agent's working directory inside the box.

path.description: The JSONL file, when `sink` is `jsonl`. Ignored by the Event Log sink.

oneOf.description:
One JSON object per line. The prototype's sink, and readable without a
SIEM.

The Windows Event Log. **v1's sink** (`docs/audit.md`): every customer's
SIEM agent already collects it, so integration work is zero. Windows
only; elsewhere the broker refuses to start with it.

BoxId.description:
Which box. From the config, carried on every audit record
(`docs/audit.md`, Fields). Not minted: a human or the platform names it.

BrokerConfig.description: Where the broker listens and what it presents.

certPin.description:
SHA-256 of the broker's leaf certificate in DER form.

The endpoint trusts this one certificate and no CA bundle at all. A
public root store here would be a way for something in the guest to be
talked into trusting a broker that is not the broker.

clientCaPath.description:
The CA whose certificates the broker accepts from clients. mTLS is
mandatory: a client without one does not complete a handshake.

url.description: The base URL the endpoint dials, e.g. `https://127.0.0.1:7580`.

ContentHash.description: A SHA-256 digest in lowercase hex. On the wire it is a bare string.

EndpointConfig.description: What the endpoint presents, and where the console listens.

clientCertPath.description: Endpoint client certificate (PEM), signed by the broker's client CA.

consoleListen.description:
Where the console's loopback API listens, e.g. `127.0.0.1:7582`.

Loopback and unauthenticated in LOCAL, which is a limitation and is
written down as one in `prototype/README.md` rather than glossed.

oneOf.description:
One laptop, an OS identity, a fixture folder and a mapped share. Proves
functionality, UI, usability and NTFS semantics; proves nothing about
identity or the guest boundary (D-010).
A demo-tenant workstation with a real signed-in user.
